sections.overviewP1: Potok is an extensible platform for decentralized plugins and UI modules in the Potok media ecosystem. Its architecture is built on strict security, declarative UI design, and isolated client-side sandbox execution.
sections.overviewP2: Unlike traditional plugins that can break host stability or security, Potok guarantees full extension isolation and provides a high-performance declarative rendering engine.
calloutItems: Declarative UI: markup is built with JS builders, compiled to a safe JSON schema, and rendered natively by the host.
Isolated sandbox: plugin code runs in an isolated context without access to browser globals.
Global slot registry: plugins mount via React Portals using CSS selectors from a single registry.
Slot inspector: built-in visual debugger for live code testing.
sections.declarativeP: Instead of manipulating the DOM or injecting untrusted HTML, plugins describe UI with builder chains (SwiftUI-like syntax). The result compiles to a safe JSON schema and is rendered by the native host engine:
sections.sandboxP: Each plugin runs inside an isolated JS sandbox:
sandboxItems: Global objects window, document, and localStorage are shadowed to undefined.
All network access goes strictly through the PotokSDK.http proxy client.
Local storage is isolated and scoped per plugin.

sections.title: Deploying Potok
sections.intro: Potok requires two services to run: the web client and the API gateway (BFF). PostgreSQL is bundled because the gateway depends on it. SearchEngine and TorrentGo are optional add-ons — add them to the same docker-compose.yml only when you install the potok-torrents plugin.
sections.requiredDesc: Web client, gateway, and PostgreSQL. This is the minimum deployment for browsing media, plugins, and the SDK wiki.
sections.optionalDesc: Append these services to the same compose file when you need torrent search and streaming (potok-torrents plugin). Configure searchEngineURL and torrentGoURL in the plugin manifest / connection profile — not via Gateway env vars.
sections.optionalNote: Without SearchEngine and TorrentGo, Potok works normally for metadata, library, and non-torrent plugins. The torrents plugin calls these services directly from the browser.
sections.runCommand: Run in the directory with docker-compose.yml:

sections.title: Plugin manifest
sections.intro: Every Potok extension must include manifest.json in its root. The host reads it for initialization, UI slots, and permissions.

rows.desc: Unique plugin identifier (e.g. potok-torrents).
Plugin name shown in the UI.
Plugin version in SemVer format (e.g. 1.0.0).
Short description of the extension purpose and features.
Author or development team.
Path to compiled JS relative to the plugin folder (usually index.js).
Extension category: sources for media sources, visual for themes, other for misc.
Requested security permissions (storage, http-proxy, ui-notifications).
UI slot contributions; each entry has id, slotName, and title.
Configurable plugin settings rendered in the host settings panel.

sections.permissionsIntro: If a plugin calls an API without the matching manifest permission, the runtime blocks the operation:
permissionsItems: storage — grants access to local DB/key storage via storage.local.
http-proxy — grants network requests via the host http proxy (CORS bypass).
ui-notifications — grants system notifications and HUD toasts (e.g. ui.showHUD()).
sections.slotsIntro: Each slots entry describes where the plugin mounts in the host UI. Supported slotName values:

rows.desc: Top section of the sidebar menu (top-level navigation).
Extra menu items near Home.
Extra menu items in Library.
Bottom of the sidebar (status/service buttons).
Action block on movie/series details (e.g. play buttons).
Panel below main media details.
Settings slot for color palette and themes.
Custom tabs in host settings.
Full-screen extension page.

sections.configIntro: The config field declares plugin settings auto-rendered in the host settings panel. Each key maps to a parameter descriptor with this structure:

rows.desc: Setting value type: "string", "boolean" (toggle), "number", "select" (dropdown), or "notice" (orange warning banner).
Default value; type must match the type field.
Label shown to the user in settings.
Another config key controlling visibility of this setting.

sections.title: State management
sections.intro: Use createState to wrap an object in a Proxy that tracks mutations and notifies subscribers for dynamic UI updates.
sections.subscriptionText: Reactive state exposes $subscribe(callback). Typically the render function is passed. $subscribe returns an unsubscribe function to prevent memory leaks:
sections.deepReactivityText: The runtime tracks nested changes. Nested objects are wrapped in proxies so deep keys and array mutations trigger updates:
sections.batchingText: Subscriber calls are batched via a microtask queue (Promise.resolve()) to avoid multiple re-renders when several fields change synchronously:
sections.reactiveExampleText: Test reactivity interactively in the sandbox with this counter example:

sections.title: Network requests
sections.intro: Plugins run in an isolated iframe where direct fetch to external APIs is blocked. PotokSDK.http proxies requests through the host.
sections.getSignature: http.get(url: string, headers?: Record<string, string>): Promise<{ status: number, data: any }>
sections.postSignature: http.post(url: string, body?: any, headers?: Record<string, string>): Promise<{ status: number, data: any }>
corsItems: CORS bypass: requests run via the Potok backend (or browser extension), removing source-server CORS blocks.
Automatic JSON parsing: JSON responses are parsed into the data field.
sections.sandboxButton: Load Todo over network in Sandbox

sections.title: Local storage
sections.intro: Use PotokSDK.storage.local for async plugin settings, tokens, and cache.

rows.desc: Asynchronously reads a key value.
Saves a value under the given key.

sections.isolationText: For security the host prefixes every stored value with pluginId. Plugin A cannot access plugin B keys. Direct window.localStorage access is blocked.

sections.title: Global ui object
sections.intro: Beyond UI builders, PotokSDK.ui controls host state, navigation, player, block mutations, and plugin registration.
sections.renderText: ui.render(component, slotId?) compiles declarative markup and sends it to the host. With slotId it mounts into that slot; otherwise it renders on the sandbox main screen.
sections.hudText: ui.showHUD(type, message) shows a short system banner. Supported types: "success", "error", "info", "warning".
sections.playerText: ui.playVideo(playbackInfo) opens the fullscreen player. The playback object should include:
sections.epSelectorText: ui.showEpisodeSelector(config) opens the system modal for picking seasons and episodes in TV shows.
sections.navigationText: ui.navigateTo(to, state?) programmatically navigates the user to another host section (settings, library, home, etc.):
sections.themesIntro: Visual plugins can register custom color schemes and switch the host accent:
themesItems: ui.registerThemes(themes: Theme[]) — registers custom theme presets on the host.
ui.setAccentTheme(themeId: string) — switches the active host accent theme.
sections.blockText: ui.block(blockName) returns a builder to mutate host UI blocks. Use element(id) to hide, edit, insert before/after, or replace; append/prepend add layout; apply() sends mutations to the host.
blockItems: element(id).before(ui) / after(ui) / replace(ui) — insert or replace layout.
append(ui) / prepend(ui) — add layout at block end or start.
apply() — registers accumulated mutations with the host.
sections.onBlockContextUpdateText: ui.onBlockContextUpdate(callback) subscribes to active block context updates. The callback receives (blockName, context) when screen data changes (e.g. another movie). Returns an unsubscribe function.
sections.registrationIntro: Global SDK functions integrate plugins into the host lifecycle:

rows.desc: Registers plugin metadata (id, name, version). Call first on script load.
Registers a media stream lookup source for host video search.
Registers UI in a named slot (e.g. media-actions, details-bottom).
Subscribes to live settings form changes; callback gets (key, value, currentSettings).
Tells the host to update settings form fields in real time; accepts { updates }.

sections.registerSlotIntro: Lets a plugin inject UI into predefined host areas. The host calls the render function when the screen mounts and draws the returned layout.
sections.registerSlotConfigIntro: The config object has these parameters:
registerSlotParams: id (string, required) — Unique contribution id matching manifest slots[].id.
render(props) (function, required) — Returns { label, icon?, layout } using UI builders.
registerSlotRenderFields: layout (UIComponent) — UI tree built with Card(), VStack(), Button(), etc.
sections.easyPluginIntro: Minimal working extension that adds a trailer button and info block on the movie details page:
sections.folderStructure:
my-easy-plugin/
├── manifest.json   # Metadata and slot declarations
└── index.js        # Plugin executable JS

sections.title: Internationalization API
sections.intro: PotokSDK.i18n lets plugins read host UI strings and register their own translation bundles. The host injects the current language and pushes updates on change.
sections.tDesc: Returns a translated string by key namespace:path for the current language. Supports {{var}} interpolation and plural forms via { count }.
sections.addResourceBundleDesc: Registers a plugin dictionary for a language and namespace. Example: addResourceBundle("en", "myplugin", { greeting: "Hi {{name}}" }).
sections.registerTranslationsDesc: Bulk registration: { en: { myplugin: {...} }, ru: { myplugin: {...} } }. Also notifies the host to persist plugin translations.
sections.onLanguageChangeDesc: Subscribe to UI language changes. Returns an unsubscribe function. Redraw plugin UI when the host language changes.
sections.languageNote: Current language is available as PotokSDK.i18n.language (e.g. "en", "ru").

sections.title: Stream sources & search
sections.intro: Plugins can register torrent/stream sources and media search providers that the host invokes when users browse streams or search the library.
sections.registerStreamSourceDesc: Registers a stream source with id, name, supportedTypes (movie | tv), and async handlers: search(query), getEpisodes(stream, context), getPlaybackInfo(stream, context). The host calls these when the user opens the streams page.
sections.searchProviderDesc: Builder for registering a library search provider: media.searchProvider(id, name).icon(url).onSearch(callback). The callback receives the query and returns search results to the host.
